Think of browser Gemini and the Windows app as two doors into the same shop. The new door may save a few steps; it does not make Gemini a different kind of tool.

Google says the app requires Windows 10 or later, 8 GB of RAM, 200 MB of disk space and internet access. You also need a personal Google Account, or a work or school account with Gemini enabled by its administrator. On a managed account, that administrator controls availability.

You can choose to upload an image or connect Google apps such as Gmail and Drive. Read what you are connecting and only share material you are comfortable using with the service.

Google announced the Windows app on September 10; it is available globally for Windows 10 and 11. Press Alt + Space to open it beside the app you are using. It brings Gemini’s quick answers, drafting and brainstorming into a window beside an active app.

Compared with Gemini in the browser, the difference is the shortcut and window beside the task. If you are revising a school-volunteer email, you could paste the draft and ask for a warmer version that keeps the date and request unchanged. You still check it before sending.

If browser Gemini already suits you, the Windows app is unnecessary. It is best suited to a small task, such as starting a simple email draft or brainstorming, when you do not want to open a tab. Google has not stated in these release notes whether the Windows app is free, paid, or included in a plan.

Before you switch, check the account you are using and decide what information you want to upload or connect.

"} EXACT PASSAGE REFERENCES: [P001] Gemini comes to Windows with an Alt + Space shortcut [P002] Google announced the Windows app on September 10; it is available globally for Windows 10 and 11. Press Alt + Space to open it beside the app you are using. It brings Gemini’s quick answers, drafting and brainstorming into a window beside an active app. [P003] Compared with Gemini in the browser, the difference is the shortcut and window beside the task. If you are revising a school-volunteer email, you could paste the draft and ask for a warmer version that keeps the date and request unchanged. You still check it before sending. [P004] Think of browser Gemini and the Windows app as two doors into the same shop. The new door may save a few steps; it does not make Gemini a different kind of tool. [P005] Google says the app requires Windows 10 or later, 8 GB of RAM, 200 MB of disk space and internet access. You also need a personal Google Account, or a work or school account with Gemini enabled by its administrator. On a managed account, that administrator controls availability. [P006] You can choose to upload an image or connect Google apps such as Gmail and Drive. Read what you are connecting and only share material you are comfortable using with the service. [P007] If browser Gemini already suits you, the Windows app is unnecessary. It is best suited to a small task, such as starting a simple email draft or brainstorming, when you do not want to open a tab. Google has not stated in these release notes whether the Windows app is free, paid, or included in a plan. [P008] Before you switch, check the account you are using and decide what information you want to upload or connect. [P009] “Gemini on Windows is mostly a faster doorway: Alt + Space opens it beside what you are doing. It is not proof that Gemini can automatically see your screen, files or every app.” [P010] A desktop app changes the route into a tool. It does not erase account controls, feature limits or the need to decide what information to share. It is not permission to imitate her voice, persona, mannerisms, identity or the structure of a particular talk or book. Her name is not evidence that a draft is clear or engaging. The LAiDIES producer must translate the useful mechanics into the cognitive job and scale of the destination. A class can support prediction, demonstration and transfer. A book can create curiosity, make a hidden process concrete and route a better next question without becoming a lecture. A reference, FAQ, practice item, interactive or NewsStand explanation uses only the moves that improve its own job. Promotional copy and microcopy declare the lens not applicable rather than manufacturing teaching. ## Communication dimensions 1. **Human question:** begin from a reason the learner already has to care, choose, notice or challenge—not from terminology for its own sake. 2. **Useful curiosity:** invite a prediction, tension, surprise or question only when the answer will reveal the mechanism. A hook without explanatory payoff fails. 3. **Invisible process made concrete:** use the smallest faithful case, demonstration, diagram, comparison or sequence that lets the learner see what otherwise happens out of view. 4. **Familiar and technical movement:** connect ordinary experience to the correct abstraction and then return to the real system. A familiar example that never reconnects to the mechanism is decoration. 5. **Limitations and consequences:** retain where the explanation stops, what can go wrong, uncertainty, misuse and why the distinction matters. 6. **Humour and surprise:** use them only when they sharpen attention, distinction or recall without making the learner or subject childish. `NOT_APPLICABLE` is often the right choice. 7. **Better next question:** leave the learner able to ask, test or notice something more precise than before. ## Default substantial-explanation arc Ali's supplied [analysis reel](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DazjzEQo4gP/) adds an ordering rule to the dimensions above. The direct Instagram fetch was throttled during the 2026-08-08 evidence check; a public [cross-platform transcript](https://tokscribe.com/t/cmrm19jj202oi140r806a97qv) records the creator's observational analysis of 30 high-performing Hannah Fry videos. Treat that analysis as a communication-pattern source, not an experimental proof of learning effectiveness. For an episode, class or substantial explanation, the default arc is: 1. **Shared starting point and live question:** begin with a physical, everyday or work experience the learner can picture, then open a precise gap she has a reason to resolve. 2. **Mechanism, link by link:** spend the centre and largest share of the explanation on cause and effect. Let the learner follow the discovery; do not substitute suspense, analogy or personality for the mechanism. 3. **Earned click:** after the mechanism, resolve the gap with the distinction, correction or consequence that makes her think “oh, I get it now.” Do not hide a direct safety-critical answer merely to manufacture a reveal. 4. **Small landing:** finish with a precise observation, useful action, better question or earned joke. Do not inflate a bounded explanation into a grand inspirational moral. This is a default explanatory sequence, not a sentence template. An FAQ, reference, breaking-news item or safety instruction may need the direct answer first; it records a proportional adaptation rather than distorting its real job to imitate a reel. ## Generation rule Before drafting, the producer records which dimensions apply, why, the exact experience or prose move planned for each, the destination-specific adaptation and the no-imitation boundary. Full explanations apply at least six dimensions and bind the four-part arc's shared starting point, curiosity gap, causal sequence, earned click and small landing. Proportional formats apply at least two dimensions and either adapt named arc moves or explain why the sequence would obstruct their job. The record fails if it merely says "Hannah Fry inspired." ## Review and learning-loop rule The producer and independent reviewer inspect the exact artifact for evidence that the applied moves improve understanding and engagement while preserving technical truth. For a full explanation, they also locate the actual starting point, causal sequence, earned click and landing in the artifact. They reject name-dropping, curiosity without payoff, a familiar example with no technical return, pastiche, a reveal before the mechanism earns it, a hook that receives more attention than the explanation, entertainment before understanding and an inflated ending. Any newly observed reusable failure follows the shared learning-disposition route; feedback cannot automatically rewrite, retire or unpublish content. ## Existing basis Version 1 consolidated the already adopted analysis in `operations/classes/CLASS-MEDIA-PRODUCTION-STANDARD.md` and `operations/product-stewards/LEARNING-CONTENT-STANDARD.md`. The research basis and its 2026-08-02 check date remain in the Classes standard. Version 2 adds Ali's 2026-08-08 ordering decision from the supplied reel analysis. Because producer contracts bind the exact benchmark bytes, this revision invalidates stale communication designs before further drafting. A future evidence refresh may revise this lens through Learning-owner admission; it may not silently change an in-flight producer contract.
